method: Second intensive review: Atomscan plus Cleave facts, Rizin/Capstone disassembly, exact-byte comparison, bounded QuickJS/Unicorn emulation. Emulation stubs all external effects. No ELF entry point or whole bundle was executed on the host; no embedded endpoint was contacted.

tooling.atomscan: Installed 2.13.0 with v18.18 models; before/after scans use CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0, --mode slow, --follow=none, no updates, no Hopper upload. Its old embedded validator rejects the already-documented metadata/file/naming=101 budget. Final full validation uses the newer local release Cleave.
tooling.baseline: Initial --follow none syntax caused dependency expansion; those archive results are excluded from the comparison. Reconstructed the original trait tree from clean HEAD into scratch, then rescanned with the same --follow=none options. Archive member sets, scores and all traits are identical before/after.
tooling.facts: Full cleave facts were collected for all three originals and the four named JavaScript members, including decoded text; all four member parsers report no errors.

samples.identification: versaWYS-PHP project skeleton 3.12.0 with legacy vendored SweetAlert2 and SheetJS
evidence: Manifest, README, PHP controllers and Vue/TypeScript dashboard implement the advertised application skeleton. No unrelated install-time payload was established.

Both supplied SweetAlert2 members have a module-load routine checking Russian navigator.language and a .ru/.su/.by/.xn--p1ai host. The first qualifying visit writes a timestamp; after more than three days a 500ms callback sets document.body.style.pointerEvents=none, appends looping remote audio, and schedules play after 2500ms. Bounded QuickJS evaluation of the exact extracted routines confirms all gates and effects with stubbed DOM, storage and timers.

The disabling assignment precedes attempted playback, so an autoplay rejection does not prevent input disruption. This behavior is unrelated to displaying a requested dialog and tips the verdict despite legitimate packaging.

The two SheetJS bundles implement ordinary spreadsheet/CFB/ZIP parsing, codecs and caller-selected filesystem read/write paths; no hostile or suspicious finding fires on either. Keep their encoding, file I/O and library findings.

The dashboard import maps currently select node_modules/sweetalert2/dist/sweetalert2.esm.all.min.js; no default template reference to the old vendored JS was found. The hostile code is nevertheless included as public executable assets. Actual deployment, user locale/host, first-visit history and whether these assets are loaded are unknown; installation-time execution and first-party malicious intent are not asserted.
samples.coverage_gap: All three retained hostile IDs describe the same supported regional-sabotage outcome, at file, archive and identity scopes. No second independent malicious behavior was established; no duplicate was added to meet a count.
samples.member_comparison: All 238 Atomscan units and all 285 source-matched Cleave units have identical before/after trait IDs and criticalities. SweetAlert2 members each retain one hostile finding; SheetJS members retain zero hostile/suspicious findings.
samples.classifier_disagreement: The calibrated ML verdict stays BENIGN for the archive and both SweetAlert2 members despite accurate hostile rule findings. This is a classifier miss; accurate traits were preserved.

samples.identification: Inert Mirai-derived mutation retaining data and two libc syscall stubs
evidence: The ELF entry remains 0x400194, but its startup and entire application .text are NOPs. Of 60534 .text bytes only 95 are non-NOP: the kill wrapper at 0x409188..0x4091b4, socket wrapper at 0x40b4fc..0x40b52b, and a four-byte trailing prologue. There is no main, credential iterator, decoder, connect/send implementation, command parser or attack dispatch.

Entry falls through NOPs into kill with uninitialized arguments. On a non-error return the wrapper ret consumes argc as a return address; the error path calls an erased errno helper. No valid startup-to-bot execution path exists.

The retained read-only tables contain IoT credentials under XOR 0x22, XOR-0x51 controller/procfs/daemon/shell text, and uClibc locale/printf data. These are real static observations, preserved at existing severities; the decoded shell child is stored content, not a reachable launch.

An existing fixture generator independently documents the exact application-erasure and stub-retention construction. Byte analysis, rather than the filename or fixture label, establishes this artifact as an inert test mutation.
samples.finding_review: All nine remaining suspicious detections describe actual device-specific credentials, an XOR-hidden dictionary, or its co-occurrence with device/BusyBox/query markers. They do not establish an executing credential scanner and remain valid despite BENIGN. The third-party Mirai fingerprint stays notable as lineage evidence.
corrections: Require connection and transmission evidence in the shared stripped Mirai identity rule. Data tables and a generic socket stub cannot establish a bot.

Remove nolibc-network-payload: zero DT_NEEDED entries plus few recovered functions establishes neither lack of static libc nor concealment; socket creation also does not establish a connection. All raw syscall atoms and metadata legs remain.
Rename nolibc-direct-syscall-binary to few-function-static-syscall-binary, preserving matcher, platform/type gates and notable severity, and update both exact consumers.
samples.classifier_disagreement: Default classification changes from HOSTILE[100%] to BENIGN[54%], verified with a live terminal scan. The raw probability remains 0.99888813 and reaches level 4000, so looser operating points can still over-call the retained malware data. Default classification agrees with the verdict.

samples.identification: Mirai-derived static x86-64 IoT credential-spraying DDoS bot with shifted loop guard
evidence: Entry 0x400194 hands main 0x405230 to libc startup. Main initializes the hidden string table, overwrites argv[0], uses prctl(PR_SET_NAME), forks/setsid, closes standard descriptors, registers attack callbacks and starts scanner 0x406690.

Table routines 0x408410/0x408490 XOR four byte lanes of eight words into bounded entries, with effective byte mask 0x51. Credentials are copied and XOR-decoded with 0x22 at 0x4064d0. The scanner builds TCP SYNs for Telnet and uses a weighted default-credential dictionary in its connection-state machine.

The C2 path bounds a two-byte network-order frame length to 1024, receives body bytes through 0x40b44c and calls 0x400410 at 0x405ba1. The parser extracts duration, vector, target count, IPv4/netmask records and options; 0x4001c0 forks a timer/attack process and dispatches the selected callback.

The supplied bytes differ from hash-verified original 4a176f94c0e73d4fcee31e0202aa973497cbc9dfc90b5739175f152424a1d5b8 only at file 0x3375: CA became CB. The jz at 0x403374 lands at 0x403341, decoding test ebp,ebp instead of test r13d,r13d at 0x403340. EBP was loaded from the unsigned payload-length word at rsp+0x2a (default 512). Positive length continues repeated target sweeps and bound sendto calls. Bounded Unicorn execution with send callbacks confirms six sends across three sweeps; a zero length or branch to the jle spin produces only one sweep.

Independent raw UDP target iteration and Telnet scanner remain intact. Static tasking and unsolicited credential guessing/flooding tip MALICIOUS; there is no supplied authorization or legitimate testing interface. Controller availability, infection success, raw-socket privilege and actual deployment are unknown.
samples.correction: Accept the shifted outer branch only when its adjacent payload-length initialization/guard and stack-slot relationship are present; retain the old target-guard alternative unchanged and preserve the bound send-wrapper target requirement.
samples.coverage: Hostile coverage increases from four to seven findings, including distinct tasking, Telnet credential spraying and UDP flood behavior. No existing trait is lost.
